svg.aria-label: Battery wiring, step by step, using the Adafruit JST-PH switch cable

text.font-family: ui-sans-serif, 'Segoe UI', Roboto, Helvetica, Arial, sans-serif

svg.text: Battery wiring — step by step

text.font-family: ui-sans-serif, 'Segoe UI', Roboto, Helvetica, Arial, sans-serif

svg.text: The battery is never cut and stays swappable. The switch is already wired into the cable, so the whole build has exactly TWO glue joints:

text.font-family: ui-sans-serif, 'Segoe UI', Roboto, Helvetica, Arial, sans-serif

svg.text: the two BAT pads on the XIAO. Everything else is a plug or a factory joint.

text.font-family: ui-sans-serif, 'Segoe UI', Roboto, Helvetica, Arial, sans-serif

svg.text: THE PART:

text.font-family: ui-sans-serif, 'Segoe UI', Roboto, Helvetica, Arial, sans-serif

svg.text: Adafruit "JST 2-pin Extension Cable with On/Off Switch — JST PH2" · ~20 in / 508 mm · 22 AWG · $7.25 · qty 1 is plenty

text.font-family: ui-sans-serif, 'Segoe UI', Roboto, Helvetica, Arial, sans-serif

svg.text: switch where you want it — flat on the

text.font-family: ui-sans-serif, 'Segoe UI', Roboto, Helvetica, Arial, sans-serif

svg.text: Strip 6 mm, fan the strands

text.font-family: ui-sans-serif, 'Segoe UI', Roboto, Helvetica, Arial, sans-serif

svg.text: 22 AWG is thick for a 1 mm pad, so

text.font-family: ui-sans-serif, 'Segoe UI', Roboto, Helvetica, Arial, sans-serif

svg.text: splay the strands into a flat fan with

text.font-family: ui-sans-serif, 'Segoe UI', Roboto, Helvetica, Arial, sans-serif

svg.text: your fingernail. More contact area,

text.font-family: ui-sans-serif, 'Segoe UI', Roboto, Helvetica, Arial, sans-serif

svg.text: less bulk, a flatter joint.

text.font-family: ui-sans-serif, 'Segoe UI', Roboto, Helvetica, Arial, sans-serif

svg.text: 6 mm

text.font-family: ui-sans-serif, 'Segoe UI', Roboto, Helvetica, Arial, sans-serif

svg.text: Do both wires. Keep the two ends apart —

text.font-family: ui-sans-serif, 'Segoe UI', Roboto, Helvetica, Arial, sans-serif

svg.text: the cell is live even with the switch OFF.

text.font-family: ui-sans-serif, 'Segoe UI', Roboto, Helvetica, Arial, sans-serif
ui-sans-serif, 'Segoe UI', Roboto, Helvetica, Arial, sans-serif

svg.text: METER before anything touches

text.font-family: ui-sans-serif, 'Segoe UI', Roboto, Helvetica, Arial, sans-serif

svg.text: Switch ON. Put the meter on DC volts

text.font-family: ui-sans-serif, 'Segoe UI', Roboto, Helvetica, Arial, sans-serif

svg.text: and touch the two bare ends. A reading

text.font-family: ui-sans-serif, 'Segoe UI', Roboto, Helvetica, Arial, sans-serif

svg.text: of +3.5 to +4.2 V means the RED probe

text.font-family: ui-sans-serif, 'Segoe UI', Roboto, Helvetica, Arial, sans-serif

svg.text: is on the positive wire. Mark it.

svg.text: aren't wired to one convention.

svg.text: Tape first, then glue

text.font-family: ui-sans-serif, 'Segoe UI', Roboto, Helvetica, Arial, sans-serif

svg.text: Clean both pads with 91% IPA. Tape the

text.font-family: ui-sans-serif, 'Segoe UI', Roboto, Helvetica, Arial, sans-serif

svg.text: wire body to the board edge so the tape

text.font-family: ui-sans-serif, 'Segoe UI', Roboto, Helvetica, Arial, sans-serif

svg.text: takes every tug. Then a small dab of

text.font-family: ui-sans-serif, 'Segoe UI', Roboto, Helvetica, Arial, sans-serif

svg.text: wire glue bridging fan → pad. Cure

text.font-family: ui-sans-serif, 'Segoe UI', Roboto, Helvetica, Arial, sans-serif

svg.text: 12–24 h, then E6000 over the top.

svg.text: + → pad FARTHER from USB-C.

svg.text: Mount it on the rear wall

text.font-family: ui-sans-serif, 'Segoe UI', Roboto, Helvetica, Arial, sans-serif

svg.text: Switch and plug junction live OUTSIDE,

text.font-family: ui-sans-serif, 'Segoe UI', Roboto, Helvetica, Arial, sans-serif

svg.text: flat on the pod's rear end wall (34.6 ×

text.font-family: ui-sans-serif, 'Segoe UI', Roboto, Helvetica, Arial, sans-serif

svg.text: 6.6 mm of free face). Wires cross the

text.font-family: ui-sans-serif, 'Segoe UI', Roboto, Helvetica, Arial, sans-serif

svg.text: wall top — the pod is an open tray.

text.font-family: ui-sans-serif, 'Segoe UI', Roboto, Helvetica, Arial, sans-serif

svg.text: pod, rear face

svg.text: switch

text.font-family: ui-sans-serif, 'Segoe UI', Roboto, Helvetica, Arial, sans-serif

svg.text: junction

text.font-family: ui-sans-serif, 'Segoe UI', Roboto, Helvetica, Arial, sans-serif

svg.text: Clear of the dovetail on both docks, and

text.font-family: ui-sans-serif, 'Segoe UI', Roboto, Helvetica, Arial, sans-serif

svg.text: on TOP when the TV stand is in use.

text.font-family: ui-sans-serif, 'Segoe UI', Roboto, Helvetica, Arial, sans-serif

svg.text: Which pad is which — from Seeed's wiki:

text.font-family: ui-sans-serif, 'Segoe UI', Roboto, Helvetica, Arial, sans-serif

svg.text: NEGATIVE is the pad CLOSEST to the USB-C port.

text.font-family: ui-sans-serif, 'Segoe UI', Roboto, Helvetica, Arial, sans-serif

svg.text: Positive is the pad farther away. The two sit ~2 mm apart — never let

text.font-family: ui-sans-serif, 'Segoe UI', Roboto, Helvetica, Arial, sans-serif

svg.text: glue bridge them, and confirm on your own board before you commit.

text.font-family: ui-sans-serif, 'Segoe UI', Roboto, Helvetica, Arial, sans-serif

svg.text: Then the gate — before you trust it in a match

text.font-family: ui-sans-serif, 'Segoe UI', Roboto, Helvetica, Arial, sans-serif

svg.text: Meter battery → pad through the switch: ≤ ~0.3 Ω (subtract your

text.font-family: ui-sans-serif, 'Segoe UI', Roboto, Helvetica, Arial, sans-serif

svg.text: probe leads). Then stream 10 minutes on battery alone with zero

text.font-family: ui-sans-serif, 'Segoe UI', Roboto, Helvetica, Arial, sans-serif

svg.text: reboots. Reboots = joint resistance → re-glue, or solder those 2 pads.

text.font-family: ui-sans-serif, 'Segoe UI', Roboto, Helvetica, Arial, sans-serif

svg.text: USB-C still charges the cell right through the cable — leave the switch ON to charge.

text.font-family: ui-sans-serif, 'Segoe UI', Roboto, Helvetica, Arial, sans-serif

svg.text: The firmware never sleeps (~60–100 mA idle), which is the whole reason the switch is there at all.
